dedupe_keys.name: green space types and accessibility in the seven largest urban regions of finland

description: Geospatial data on green space types and how far people must walk or cycle to reach them in the seven largest urban regions of Finland, produced by the Finnish Environment Institute Syke and described in a 2023 Data in Brief article by Vuokko Heikinheimo, Maija Tiitu and Arto Viinikka. Green space types come from the Urban Atlas data and were enhanced with Finnish national data on water bodies, conservation areas and recreational facilities and routes. Path distances were computed on the walkable street network from OpenStreetMap with open-source Python tools, up to ten kilometres from each green space edge, then aggregated into a 250 m by 250 m statistical grid that can be joined to Finnish statistics. The Zenodo repository, published on 29 March 2023, holds GeoPackage files of green spaces, water bodies and accessibility, a CSV of accessibility of about 52 MB, a QGIS project and a README, plus the processing scripts. Coverage: seven urban regions in Finland. Licence: CC BY 4.0; cost free. Caveats: accessibility is based on 2018 Urban Atlas and OpenStreetMap paths as of the study, and files are large. Useful for equity, adaptation and planning models of public space; it relates to the catalogued large public urban green space indicators for 13 cities.
